note: `background-clip: text`, also spelled `-webkit-background-clip: text`, fills the text with the background color and gradient layers, as Tailwind's `bg-clip-text text-transparent` expects. `-webkit-text-fill-color: transparent` works too.
`::first-letter` rules match nothing yet.
`::first-line` rules match nothing yet.

`font-palette: normal | light | dark | <name>` and `@font-palette-values` (`font-family`, `base-palette`, `override-colors`) recolor COLR fonts, version 0 and 1. `palette-mix()` is not supported and draws the normal palette. `@font-palette-values` inside `@media` or `@supports` is ignored.
Every `@font-face` behaves as `font-display: swap`: text draws with the fallback until the face loads, then reshapes. `block`, `fallback` and `optional` are ignored.
`font-stretch` and `font-width` pick the nearest width among a family's faces and set the `wdth` axis of a variable font.
`hanging-punctuation` is ignored; punctuation stays inside the line box.
`hyphens: manual` and `none` work. `auto` breaks only at soft hyphens (`­`), like `manual`: there are no hyphenation dictionaries.
`initial-letter` is ignored, and `::first-letter`, which it styles, matches nothing.
`text-box`, `text-box-trim` and `text-box-edge` are ignored; line boxes keep the font's full ascent and descent.

`text-wrap: balance` evens out the lines of plain text, up to six lines, and aligns them in the full width. Text beside floats or broken across columns or pages, and `text-wrap: pretty`, wrap like `wrap`.
About pages and printing. They are honored when a host lays out pages (`frameFragmented`); an app's continuous layout never breaks a paragraph across pages.

`ui-sans-serif`, `ui-serif`, `ui-monospace` and `ui-rounded` use the families the host sets for them (on macOS the system loader sets San Francisco, New York, SF Mono and SF Pro Rounded), then stand in for `system-ui`, `serif`, `monospace` and `system-ui`.
`system-ui` picks the platform's interface font from the installed fonts: San Francisco on macOS, Segoe UI on Windows, then Noto Sans or DejaVu Sans.
There is no `FontFace` constructor or `document.fonts` in a JS app. Declare faces with `@font-face`; they load when text needs them.

Each face is scaled so its `ex-height` (the default), `cap-height`, `ch-width`, `ic-width` or `ic-height` is the given fraction of `font-size`, so fallback faces match the first font. `from-font` takes the first available font's own aspect.

`-webkit-font-smoothing: none` and `font-smooth: never` draw aliased glyphs. `antialiased`, `grayscale` and `subpixel-antialiased` all draw the grayscale antialiasing text always gets, as Chrome on macOS does.
A face is requested only when text uses a character in its `unicode-range`; until then the next family draws it.

`historical-forms`, `stylistic()`, `styleset()`, `character-variant()`, `swash()`, `ornaments()` and `annotation()` turn on their OpenType features, with names from `@font-feature-values`. A name resolves in the first family of `font-family` that defines it. `@font-feature-values` inside `@media` or `@supports` is ignored.
`src` takes `url()` (loaded by the host) and `local()` (an installed font); `unicode-range`, media conditions and cascade layers apply.
Kerning and ligatures are always on (turn them off with `font-kerning` or `font-feature-settings`); `text-rendering` is accepted and changes nothing.
`text-emphasis` and its longhands are ignored; no emphasis marks are drawn.
About mobile browsers enlarging the text of pages made for desktops. An app's text is drawn at the size it asks for.
`-webkit-text-fill-color` fills the glyphs, while decorations, borders and `currentcolor` keep following `color`. `-webkit-text-stroke` is ignored: glyphs get no outline.
